 " class="fuel_embeded_code_2641197"> 
 Several federal and state tax payments deadlines have been postponed since parts of Indiana were declared a federal disaster area.  
 Tom Bayer, a CPA with Sikich LLP , says the tax relief available to Hoosiers following the August flooding in Indiana applies to 21 counties. He says the declaration provided eligible taxpayers with additional time to file certain tax returns and make payments without incurring penalties or interest.  
 Bayer says under the relief guidance, eligible taxpayers with filing deadlines falling within the covered period beginning August 11 can postpone qualifying filings and payments until February 1, 2027. He says this primarily affects individuals and businesses that filed for extensions, including certain pass-through businesses whose extended deadlines typically fall in September or October.  
 In addition, Bayer says the relief also applies to qualifying estimated tax payments, including the third-quarter payment due in September and the fourth-quarter payment scheduled for January 15, 2027. He says eligibility is not necessarily limited to taxpayers who personally live or operate within one of the 21 designated counties. Federal relief may also be available to taxpayers whose tax records are located in an affected county or whose tax preparer operates there, even if the taxpayer lives or conducts business elsewhere. However, taxpayers who qualify through these circumstances may need to contact the IRS to request the relief.
